relationships.subject: Ifnar1
relationships.evidence_quote: Therefore, host IFN-I signaling through Ifnar1 is required for the protective effects of STING agonists on cancer pain and bone destruction induced by bone cancer.

relationships.subject: DMXAA
relationships.evidence_quote: Taken together, these data indicate that STING activation with DMXAA can suppress cancer-induced hyperexcitability of DRG nociceptors.

key_findings: STING agonists attenuate bone cancer pain, bone destruction and locomotor impairment, dependent on STING and IFN-I signaling.
STING activation directly reduces cancer-induced DRG nociceptor hyperexcitability.
